analysis:
All changes are in test code under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live. None touch production sources.

GPTOSSCheckpointRestartLiveTests.swift (head lines 92-110, 163-164): the batched-donor live test now passes GPTOSSCheckpointRestartFixture.sdkPrefillGeometry as an environment to makeBridge for both the donor and restored bridges. This pins the SDK prompt geometry so the test still exercises the cap change. The comment says production GPT-OSS keeps 2,048 throughout. The change is test-only and gated behind DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_GPTOSS_CHECKPOINT_RESTART.

ModelCheckpointStorageSpecificationTests.swift (head lines 75-76): adds assertions that a pinned solo stripe also sets prefillChunkKey=512 and stepTokenBudgetKey=2048.

ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift (patch only; the file's text units were not supplied): checkpointEnvironment now also sets the prefill chunk and step token budget from CBv2SchedulerConfig() defaults, but only when a stripe is pinned. The environment is for benchmark fixtures; the cache keys stay the same (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, ..._TEST_ROOT, ..._ALLOW_EPHEMERAL). It does not alter the T-041 production gate, TTL, HMAC name derivation, DBK3 AAD, salt scoping or purge points. The tests continue to assert that wrong-tenant and changed-prefix requests get zero cache hits, so cache scope isolation is still checked.

No new attack surface, no weakened mitigation, and no threat-model invalidation identified. The one residual gap is that I did not see the full ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift text or the sdkPrefillGeometry definition in the fixture. The patch shows only the benign environment-key additions, so I do not believe this affects any security conclusion.
